original_value: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are being increasingly viewed as valuable tools to aid the management of farms. This kind of technology can be particularly useful in the context of extensive cattle farming, as production areas tend to be expansive and animals tend to be more loosely monitored. With the advent of deep learning, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in particular, extracting relevant information from aerial images has become more effective. Despite the technological advancements in drone, imaging and machine learning technologies, the application of UAVs for cattle monitoring is far from being thoroughly studied, with many research gaps still remaining. In this context, the objectives of this study were threefold: (1) to determine the highest possible accuracy that could be achieved in the detection of animals of the Canchim breed, which is visually similar to the Nelore breed (Bos taurus indicus); (2) to determine the ideal ground sample distance (GSD) for animal detection; (3) to determine the most accurate CNN architecture for this specific problem. The experiments involved 1853 images containing 8629 samples of animals, and 15 different CNN architectures were tested. A total of 900 models were trained (15 CNN architectures × 3 spacial resolutions × 2 datasets × 10-fold cross validation), allowing for a deep analysis of the several aspects that impact the detection of cattle using aerial images captured using UAVs. Results revealed that many CNN architectures are robust enough to reliably detect animals in aerial images even under far from ideal conditions, indicating the viability of using UAVs for cattle monitoring.

result.paraphrase: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly recognized as useful tools for farm management. They are especially valuable in extensive cattle production, where grazing areas are large and animals are monitored less closely. With deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), relevant information can now be extracted from aerial imagery more effectively. Even so, despite advances in drones, imaging, and machine learning, UAV-based cattle monitoring remains poorly studied and still has many gaps in the literature. Against this backdrop, the study had three aims: (1) to find the highest achievable accuracy for detecting Canchim cattle, which closely resemble the Nelore breed (Bos taurus indicus); (2) to identify the optimal ground sample distance (GSD) for animal detection; and (3) to determine the most accurate CNN architecture for this task. The experiments used 1,853 images containing 8,629 animal samples, and 15 different CNN architectures were evaluated. In total, 900 models were trained (15 CNN architectures × 3 spatial resolutions × 2 datasets × 10-fold cross-validation), enabling a detailed assessment of the factors affecting cattle detection in UAV-captured aerial images. The results showed that many CNN architectures are robust enough to detect animals reliably in aerial images even under far from ideal conditions, supporting the viability of UAVs for cattle monitoring.
